hood_desc: The compact historic core with half-timbered German-style houses, Theatre Square, and the Danė River waterfront, walkable and full of cafés.
The main commercial district beyond the old walls, with shopping streets, the central market, and everyday city life.
A quiet seaside residential area north of downtown with a long sandy beach popular with locals for evening walks.
Reached by ferry across the harbor strait, this forested spit area holds the Sea Museum, dolphinarium, and dunes leading toward Nida.
A riverside strip near the old fishing harbor that has become the city's bar and restaurant hub, especially lively in summer.

tip.r: Tipping isn't obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% in restaurants is a welcome gesture for good service.

landmarks: Theatre Square and Ännchen von Tharau Statue
The old Prussian heart of Klaipėda centres on the Drama Theatre and the beloved statue of Ännchen von Tharau, heroine of a German love song.
Old Town Fachwerk Warehouses
Cobbled lanes lined with half-timbered German merchant warehouses reveal the city's seven centuries as Memel, the Baltic's northernmost Prussian port.
Meridianas Sailing Ship
This graceful 1948 barquentine moored on the Danė River is Klaipėda's floating symbol, glowing romantically in evening lights along the embankment.
Curonian Spit (Smiltynė)
A five-minute ferry crosses to the UNESCO-listed spit's pine forests, wandering dunes and Baltic beaches stretching toward Nida's lighthouse.
Lithuanian Sea Museum and Dolphinarium
Housed in a 19th-century fortress on Smiltynė, this popular museum pairs aquariums and maritime history with penguin and dolphin residents.
Klaipėda Castle Site and Museum 39/45
The excavated bastions of the Teutonic Order's Memel castle host museums tracing the port's turbulent medieval and wartime history.
Black Ghost Sculpture (Juodasis Vaiduoklis)
A hooded bronze spectre hauls itself from the harbour water by lantern light, the most photographed of Klaipėda's playful street sculptures.
Clock and Watch Museum
A branch of the national art museum charts timekeeping from sundials to atomic clocks, with a courtyard carillon that chimes on weekends.
Martynas Mažvydas Sculpture Park
The city's former cemetery became an open-air gallery of 116 modernist Lithuanian sculptures scattered among leafy strolling paths.
Central Post Office
A splendid red-brick neo-Gothic pile from 1893, its 44-metre tower holding a carillon of 48 bells, ranks among Klaipėda's finest Prussian-era buildings.

train.note: Klaipeda's railway station is on Priestocio gatve next to the bus station, about a kilometre from the old town. LTG Link runs several trains a day to Vilnius (roughly 4.5 hours) via Kaunas and Silale or Siauliai, with cheap advance fares online. No international passenger train serves Klaipeda: for Poland you travel to Kaunas or Vilnius and pick up the cross-border service through Mockava to Bialystok and Warsaw, and the lines towards Latvia and the Kaliningrad exclave carry no passenger services from here. The seasonal summer trains to Palanga and the coast are worth checking in July and August.

intl.to: Riga (Latvia), Tallinn (Estonia), Warsaw, Lodz & Prague (Poland / Czechia) - from Klaipeda bus station, Butku Juzes g. 9

bus.note: The bus station adjoins the railway station at Butku Juzes g. 9, a 5-10 minute walk from the old town and the ferry landing. FlixBus reaches around 27 destinations from here, including Riga, Tallinn, Warsaw and Prague, and other Baltic coach operators such as Ecolines (https://ecolines.net/) also use the terminal. Domestic coaches run frequently to Vilnius (about 4 hours), Kaunas (3 hours), Siauliai and the resorts at Palanga (40 minutes) and Nida; tickets for these are sold at the counters and through the national portal at https://www.autobusubilietai.lt/. Buses to Riga take about 5 hours and cross an internal Schengen border with no routine checks.

intl.to: Kiel (Germany) - from the international ferry terminal north of the centre, about 20 hr
Smiltyne, Curonian Spit (Lithuania) - 10 min from the Old Ferry Terminal on Zvejų gatve

ferry.note: Klaipeda is Lithuania's only seaport and the DFDS ships to Kiel and Karlshamn use the international terminal a few kilometres north of the centre, reached by taxi or local bus; both are overnight Ro-Pax sailings with cabins, and they carry a lot of freight, so book a cabin and any vehicle well ahead in summer. Crossing times are around 20 hours to Kiel and 14 to Karlshamn, with sailings most days but not daily. Separately, the little Old Ferry Terminal in the centre runs a ten-minute shuttle across the lagoon to Smiltyne on the Curonian Spit for foot passengers and cyclists, while cars use the New Ferry Terminal further south; both are operated by Smiltynes perkela and run all year.

half.name: Palanga
half.blurb: A Baltic seaside resort with a 19th-century amber-collector's palace, now an amber museum, and a pier stretching into the sea.

half.name: Nida
half.blurb: Thomas Mann's summer house and the Parnidis sand dune sit in this fishing village near the Russian border on the Curonian Spit.

half.name: Nemunas Delta (Rusnė)
half.blurb: Wetlands at the mouth of the Nemunas River draw storks and other waterbirds across a low-lying delta of channels and floodplain.
